claims.statement: The backend money model uses two representations: raw numeric values (prices, position quantity and average_cost) are `Decimal` in the API types, while any currency-tagged amount is `stockholm.Money`; `Account.currency` and `Security.currency` are `stockholm.currency.Currency`, but read models downgrade currency to plain `str` (`HoldingRead.currency`, `AccountHoldingsRead.currency`) and `AccountSchema` uses an explicit `@field_serializer("currency")` to emit its `Currency` as a code string, so `Currency` survives only in the service layer and the write path.

A `stockholm.Money` serializes to JSON as a single currency-suffixed string field (for example `{"value": "500.00 USD"}`), not as structured `units`/`nanos`/`currencyCode`; tests assert `payload["totals"]["cost"]["value"] == "500.00 USD"` and that `result["cost"]["value"]` ends with `" CAD"`.

Currency conversion is centralized in `PositionService._currency_convert`, which short-circuits when source and target currency codes match and otherwise calls `currency_converter.CurrencyConverter.convert(...)`, rounds to 2 decimal places, and re-wraps the result as `Money`; the `CurrencyConverter` instance is constructed once in `position_service_factory` and injected into the service.

Conversion is applied per position before accumulation rather than to stored values, so positions never have their `average_cost` rewritten by FX and every accumulator for total cost, total value, and total P&L adds only account-currency `Money` values.

`HoldingRead` reports the same logical amounts twice — native values in `security_currency` (`unconverted_total_value`, `latest_price`, `average_cost`, `unconverted_profit_loss`) and converted values in the account `currency` (`total_value`, `profit_loss`, `converted_average_cost`, `converted_latest_price`) — and the holdings table only prints the converted line when `holding.security_currency !== holding.currency`; `security_currency` is actually `position.currency or security.currency`, so a position-level currency overrides the security's throughout the cost and holding math.

`get_total_for_account` returns `AccountTotals(cost, value)` where `cost` is the sum of `quantity × average_cost` and `value` is the sum of `quantity × latest close`, each product rounded to 2 places and converted per position, plus a converted `free_cash` contribution added to both sides; the type is served by `GET /accounts/{account_id}/totals` and pushed over WebSocket as `AccountTotalsUpdatedMessage` by the `recalculate_all_account_totals_task` Huey task, but the frontend does not listen for that message — it still fetches totals over HTTP and only handles `sync_started`/`sync_finished`/`sync_failed`.

When `account.net_deposits` is not `None`, `AccountHoldingsRead.total_profit_loss` is overridden to `total_value - Money(net_deposits, account.currency)` — a cash-flow P&L, not a cost-basis figure — with `total_profit_loss_percent` reported only when `net_deposits != 0`; this is a distinct quantity from the per-holding `profit_loss` (value minus cost basis) and from `AccountTotals.cost`, and the asset test asserts `total_value == 1500`, `total_profit_loss == 500` and `total_profit_loss_percent == 50.0` for `1500 - 1000`.

The frontend `Money` interface is `{ value?: string; units?: number; nanos?: number; currencyCode?: string }`, and `moneyToNumber` prefers `units + nanos / 1e9` when `units` is a number, otherwise falls back to `parseFloat(value)`, returning `0` for null, undefined, or unparseable input; `money(m)` renders `$<localized number>`.

Because the API emits `value` strings like `"500.00 CAD"` with no `units`, the `units`/`nanos` branch of `moneyToNumber` is unused against the live backend and real responses succeed only because `parseFloat` stops at the first non-numeric character; frontend test fixtures supply `units`/`nanos` alongside `value`, so the units path only looks alive in tests, and a serializer or parser change on either side must update both the backend shape and the frontend `Money` type together or amounts silently become wrong or `0`.

`blendedAverageCost` computes the quantity-weighted mean of `average_cost` across holdings, returning `0` for an empty list, zero total quantity, or all-missing costs, and treating a missing `average_cost` as `0` so an unknown-cost holding pulls the blended figure toward zero rather than being excluded.

Holdings period math runs on JS `number`: `getBenchmarkPrice` returns the average cost for `period === 'ALL'` and otherwise the close of the most recent candle at or before the period cutoff (falling back to the earliest candle), and `calculateHoldingGain` returns `gainAmount = (currentPrice - benchmarkPrice) * quantity` and `gainPercent = priceDiff / benchmarkPrice * 100` guarded to `0` when the benchmark is `0`.

Precision is lost at defined storage boundaries: `PositionModel.quantity` is `DECIMAL(16, 8)` but `PositionModel.average_cost` is `Float` and `PositionModel.currency` a nullable `String(3)`, `AccountModel.currency` is a plain `String` (while the service-layer API type is `Currency`), and `AccountModel.net_deposits` and `AccountModel.free_cash` are `Float`, so cash-flow P&L and the cash contribution to both totals inherit float error.

`src/account/csv/parser.py` parses quantities and book values as `Decimal` after stripping `,` and `$`, and computes `average_cost` as `(book_value / quantity).quantize(Decimal("0.0001"), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)`, returning `None` for non-positive quantity or missing book value.

`get_holdings_by_security` computes `account_percentage` from `MarketPricesApi.get_latest_close` multiplied by quantity, rounded to 2 places, converted to the account currency, then divided by `get_total_for_account(...).value.amount`, so numerator and denominator are both in account currency only because the holding value is converted first.

CSV import currency selection and update affect aggregates: `chosen_currency` is the trimmed, upper-cased per-account value from the import request, else the currency the CSV parser derived (which itself falls back to `CAD` when a row carries no currency column and no `book_value_currency_*`/`market_price_currency` value), else `CAD`; an existing account's currency is updated when it differs from `chosen_currency`, and new accounts are created with `currency=Currency(chosen_currency)`.

The `account_totals_success` router test exercises `GET /accounts/{account_id}/totals` and asserts the returned `cost` and `value` money strings carry the ` CAD` suffix, while `test_account_totals_not_found` and `test_account_totals_not_owned` assert 404 rather than a currency payload.

Because the FX conversion target is the account's own `currency` (passed as `account.currency` into every `_currency_convert` call site), changing an account's currency re-bases every converted total, value, and P&L for that account without modifying any stored position; CSV import is one path that does this, updating an existing account's currency when a different `chosen_currency` is supplied.

`account.free_cash`, wrapped as `Money(free_cash, account.currency)` and converted, is added to both `AccountTotals.cost` and `AccountTotals.value` in `get_total_for_account` and to `total_value` in `get_account_holdings` before the net-deposits override, so reported totals and the cash-flow P&L include cash and `AccountTotals.cost` stops being a pure cost basis once cash is non-zero — which also means every consumer of `AccountTotals.value`, including `get_holdings_by_security`'s `account_percentage` denominator, is measuring cash plus holdings.

Per-position products are rounded to 2 decimal places before conversion or accumulation: `_compute_cost` rounds `quantity × average_cost`, `_compute_price` rounds `quantity × latest close`, `_calculate_holding` rounds the native value and cost, and `get_holdings_by_security` rounds quantity × latest close before converting, and `_currency_convert` rounds each converted amount before accumulation, so every aggregate is a sum of rounded per-position values rather than the rounded sum of exact values.

Missing prices and missing FX rates fail differently. A missing price is silently valued at zero (`_compute_price` and `_calculate_holdings` substitute `Money(0, security.currency)`, `_calculate_holding` reports `latest_price = 0.0` with a `None` `price_date`, and `get_holdings_by_security` falls back to `0.0` and returns an empty list with `total == 0` when the security lookup raises `SecurityNotFoundError`). A missing FX rate is not handled at all: `_currency_convert` has no fallback and lets the `currencyconverter` error propagate, so `GET /accounts/{account_id}/totals` fails the request while `_recalculate_all_account_totals` catches per account, logs, and continues.

`total-profit-loss-buttons.svelte` is the live renderer for account totals: it converts its `Money | number` props with `moneyToNumber`, derives the return percentage as `(profitLoss / cost) * 100` when not supplied, falls back to `Money.currencyCode` for the display currency, and formats with `Intl.NumberFormat('en-CA', { style: 'currency', currency })`; the `money()` helper in `money.ts` renders a bare `$` with no currency code and no fixed decimals and has no production caller (only `money.test.ts` imports it), while the holdings views use the same explicit-currency `Intl.NumberFormat` helper because they mix security and account currencies.

`holding-group.svelte` sums `moneyToNumber(totals.value)` across every account into one `totalPortfolioValue` and divides the security's `AccountHoldingRead.total_value` by it to derive `portfolioPercentage`, mixing account-currency totals (which include `free_cash`) with a numerator in the security's currency, so the ratio is only meaningful when every account shares the currency of the security being viewed.

`PriceModel` stores `open`, `high`, `low`, `close` and `adjusted_close` as `DECIMAL(16, 8)`, and user-entered price fields share that convention — `PriceAlertModel.target_price` and `SecurityValuationModel.lower_bound`/`upper_bound` are also `DECIMAL(16, 8)`, while their write schemas accept an unconstrained `Decimal` and the frontend `ValuationClient` types both bounds as plain `number`, so 8 fractional digits is the effective precision and the database, not validation, rounds anything more precise.
